sentences.text: Yunguisaurus is an extinct genus of pistosaur found in Guizhou Province, China.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is an articulated, nearly complete skeleton missing only the far end of the tail.
This main skeleton measures about 1.7 meters, with an estimated total length of 2.3 meters, while a larger paratype specimen reaches around 4.2 meters.
The generic name Yunguisaurus is derived from the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau, abbreviated as the Yungi Plateau, and the suffix 'saurus' means 'lizard' in Greek.
The specific name liae honors Professor Jinling Li for his contributions to the study of Chinese Triassic marine vertebrate fauna.
Fossils were collected near the Huangnihe River in Chajiang, Guizhou, from the Falang Formation.
Yunguisaurus was first named by Yen-Nien Cheng, Tamaki Sato, Xiao-Chun Wu, and Chun Li in 2006, with Yunguisaurus liae as the type species.
The original description of Yunguisaurus remains a preliminary report because the postcranial skeleton has not yet been fully prepared or described.
Yunguisaurus belongs to the parent group Pistosauroidea.
Yunguisaurus is classified within the class Reptilia.
Yunguisaurus is distinguished from other pistosauroids by a unique combination of anatomical characters.
Yunguisaurus lived during the Carnian stage of the early Late Triassic.
However, other data suggest it lived between 241.464 and 237 million years ago during the Ladinian stage.
